headline: High: TREK’s collaborative, MCP-enabled planner can ingest Kestra outputs and secrets-bearing workflows, creating default-path data leakage and cascading action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can write files, emit logs, and use stdin/stdout, while TREK is real-time collaborative and uses MCP. That creates a plausible bridge where Kestra-generated content could be consumed by TREK as instructions or tool input. No direct shared channel is documented, so I choose medium rather than low because the interaction is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF Kestra outputs are forwarded into TREK via MCP, WebSocket, or copied files
IF TREK parses imported notes, messages, or documents as actionable instructions
mitigations: Disable any automatic import from Kestra outputs into TREK
Add a manual review step before TREK acts on external text
Restrict MCP tools to read-only for imported content
Tag Kestra-generated artifacts as untrusted
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between the systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. TREK handles API keys, MFA secrets, email addresses, and confirmation numbers. If they share a workspace or exchange files, sensitive TREK data can flow into Kestra outputs or egress paths by default, making leakage materially dangerous.
conditions: IF TREK secrets or reservations are written into files or logs accessible to Kestra
IF Kestra sends workflow contents or artifacts to external services over broad egress
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Redact secrets before any handoff to Kestra
Disable or restrict Kestra egress for sensitive workflows
Store TREK secrets outside shared directories
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and spawn_subprocesses; TREK is collaborative and stores data in local files and logs. If both operate on the same directory or shared mutable resources, concurrent writes can corrupt workflows, travel.db, uploads, or logs. The profiles show overlapping write surfaces and no locking mechanism, so the conflict is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or database
IF TREK sessions and Kestra workflows modify shared files without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Make shared files read-only for one agent
Back up mutable data before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate logs, artifacts, and workflow outputs, and TREK is a real-time collaborative app with AI built in. If TREK treats Kestra output as authoritative, an upstream mistake can cascade into incorrect travel plans, reservations, or user-facing actions. Because the profiles show no verification boundary, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF TREK consumes Kestra-produced artifacts without validation
IF Kestra outputs are used to create or modify reservations, budgets, or user messages
mitigations: Require human approval before TREK acts on Kestra output
Validate Kestra outputs against schema and source data
Mark Kestra outputs as advisory only
Log provenance for every imported field
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra processes workflow definitions, logs, database data, and cloud storage data, while TREK handles travel plans, country visit history, user accounts, email addresses, and MFA secrets. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if personal travel data is moved into Kestra logs or cloud-backed workflows. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF personal travel data is copied into Kestra logs or artifacts
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems for the same records
mitigations: Minimize personal data passed from TREK to Kestra
Set short log retention on Kestra workflows
Document which system is system-of-record for each data class
Purge shared artifacts after completion
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
